steps.text: Play the track. Double-click anywhere on the display to add a band.
Drag the dot up. You're boosting that frequency. Drag it left and right while you listen: hear how the sound changes?
steps.check: the band's gain or frequency changed

steps.text: Scroll on the dot to change Q, the width. Narrow is focused, wide is gentle.
Click Bypass a few times to compare with and without.
Leave auto-gain on. It keeps the level the same, so you hear the tone change and not just a volume change.
Done. Remember: small moves, judged in the full mix. Next, try a recipe for this track type.
Set the track type to Bass.
Play a part where some notes boom louder than others. Watch for a peak marker between 60 and 300 Hz.
Click the marker. No marker? Double-click near the boomy area to add a band, then drag it up a lot and sweep left and right until the boom jumps out. Then bring it back to 0.
steps.check: a band exists between 60 and 300 Hz

steps.text: Right-click the band and choose Make Dynamic. Set range to about −5 dB.
steps.check: that band is dynamic with negative range

steps.text: Press Learn and keep playing for 8 seconds.
Set attack around 10 ms and release around 120 ms. Low notes need slower times.
Watch the activity number. Between 10 and 40% means it's catching only the boomy notes.
Turn on Delta for a moment. You should hear just the boom, not the whole bass. Turn it off.
Now listen with the full mix and flip bypass. The bass should feel steadier, not thinner.
Set the track type to Vocal.
steps.check: track type is Vocal or Choir & Vocal Bus

steps.text: Add a band around 6 to 7 kHz. Make it dynamic, Q around 3, range −6 dB.
steps.check: a dynamic band between 4 and 10 kHz

steps.text: Turn on Custom detector and set it to 5 kHz–10 kHz, so it listens only to the S range.
steps.check: Custom on, HP 4–6 kHz, LP 8–12 kHz

steps.text: Press Listen. You'll hear what the detector hears: mostly S's. Move the band's frequency until the S's sound sharpest, then turn Listen off.
Press Learn while the singer sings.
Set attack 1 ms, release about 50 ms. S's are fast.
Check with Delta: you should hear only S's and T's. If you hear words, reduce the range.
Listen in the mix. The vocal should still sound clear, just less sharp. If it sounds lispy, you went too far.
Put LENS on the bass track. In Logic, set the Side Chain menu at the top of the plugin window to the kick track.
Add a band where the kick thumps, around 50 to 80 Hz. Make it dynamic, Q about 1.5, range −5 dB.
steps.check: a dynamic band between 40 and 120 Hz

steps.text: Set the detector to External. Now the kick controls this band.
Turn on Custom and set it to 40–120 Hz, so only the kick's thump triggers it.
Press Learn while the song plays.
Attack 1 ms, release about 100–150 ms. Longer release for slower songs.
Listen to kick and bass together and flip bypass. The kick should punch through without the bass getting smaller.

title: Clear a pocket for the vocal

steps.text: Put LENS on the guitars, keys, or their bus. Set the Side Chain menu to the lead vocal.
Add a broad band around 2 to 3 kHz, where vocals are clearest. Make it dynamic, Q about 1, range −3 dB.
steps.check: a dynamic band between 1.5 and 4 kHz

steps.text: Set the detector to External.
Press Learn while the vocal sings.
Attack around 10 ms, release around 200 ms, so it moves smoothly with phrases.
Listen: when the singer comes in, the vocal should read clearer while the guitars still sound full. If you notice the guitars ducking, reduce the range.
Play a loud section. Harshness usually lives between 2 and 5 kHz.
Add a band, drag it up about 10 dB with a narrow Q, and sweep left and right. Stop where it sounds most painful.
steps.check: a band between 1.5 and 6 kHz with gain > +6 dB

steps.text: Now flip it: drag the gain to −4 dB and widen the Q to about 2.
Make it dynamic so it only cuts when the harshness happens.
Press Learn during a loud part.
Attack 2–5 ms, release 60–100 ms. Check activity: 10–40% is the sweet spot.
Flip bypass in the mix. Hard hits should feel less painful while soft parts sound the same.
Put LENS on the stereo output, before the limiter. Set the track type to Master.
Optional: switch to Linear Phase. For mastering it keeps everything in time across frequencies.
Add a low cut at 20–25 Hz, 12 dB/oct, to clear sub rumble.
steps.check: a Low Cut between 15 and 35 Hz

steps.text: If the low end swells on some notes, add a dynamic low shelf at about 120 Hz, range −2 dB, and press Learn.
For more air, add a high shelf at 10–12 kHz, +1 to +1.5 dB, Q 0.7. Then add a dynamic bell at 3–5 kHz, range −2 dB, to catch harshness the air might bring out.
Keep auto-gain on. Check the loudness difference: it should be near 0.
A/B against bypass, then play a song you love that's similar. Does yours sit in the same neighborhood?
Finally, listen on something else: earbuds, a car, a phone. If a move only sounds good on one system, make it smaller.
